9 June, 2023
The Hon'Ble Sri Justice Mummineni Sudheer Kumar
 Writ Petition No.36006 Of 2022
Order:

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Heard Sri P. Lakshma Reddy, learned counsel for the petitioner and learned Assistant Government Pleader for Land Acquisition appearing for the respondents Nos.1 to 5 and Sri D.V. Srinivas Rao,
learned counsel appearing for the respondent No.6.
2.

This Writ Petition is filed questioning letter No. A/7035/2016-4, dated 30-05-2022 of the respondent No.4 addressed to the Presiding Officer, Land Acquisition Rehabilitation and Resettlement Authority referring the matter under Section 77(2) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act, 2013') as illegal and arbitrary.

entities.label: ORG

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
3. The brief facts that are necessary for disposal of the Writ Petition are as under:
4.

The respondent No.2 initiated proceedings for acquisition of land situated in Sy.No.385/A2 and Sy.No.385/E2 admeasuring Acs.5-08 guntas and Ac.0-11 guntas respectively 2 MSK,J W.P.NO.36006 OF 2022 of Indaram Village, Jaipur Mandal, Mancherial District by issuing primary notification under Section 11 of the Act, 2013 through proceedings No.C2/1374/2019, dated 28.08.2019 and declaration was made under Section 19(1) of the Act, 2013 through proceedings No.C2/1374/2019, dated 23.12.2019.
The name of the petitioner herein was notified as a person entitled to receive compensation in respect of the said extent of land.

At that stage, the respondent No.6 herein filed objections and also made a claim for payment of compensation for the said land in his favour and during the pendency of the said proceedings, respondent No.6 herein has approached this Court by filing W.P.No.13753 of 2020 seeking a direction for consideration of the objections filed by him before the respondent No.2 in the said acquisition proceedings.
The respondent No.4 filed counter affidavit stating that the objections filed by the respondent No.6 were already rejected by passing an order, dated 31.12.2020.

Thereafter, during the pendency of the said Writ Petition, the impugned letter came to be issued by the respondent No.2 referring the matter to the Authority under Section 77(2) of the Act, 2013 on the ground that respondent No.6 herein filed W.P.No. 13753 of 2020 before this Court and the same is pending for consideration.

Having been aggrieved by the said letter dated 13.05.2022, the petitioner approached this Court by filing the present Writ Petition contending that the objections raised by the respondent No.6 were already rejected by the respondent No.2 by passing an order dated 31.12.2020 and that the said order has become final and the respondent No.6 has not taken any steps for questioning the said Kadari Satayanarayana Reddy , ... vs The State Of Telangana on 9 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/21980004/
1 order and thus, it is contended that, as the objections raised by the respondent No.6 were already rejected and the same had become final, there is no justification for respondent No.2 to refer the matter under Section 77(2) of the Act, 2013 to the Authority through the impugned letter.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is also brought to the notice of this Court by the learned counsel for the petitioner that W.P.No.13753 of 2020 filed by the respondent No.6 herein was also dismissed as withdrawn by order, dated 18.01.2023 with a liberty to the petitioner to avail remedies otherwise available under law.

According to the learned counsel for the petitioner, even after dismissal of the said Writ Petition as withdrawn, the respondent No.6 has not taken any steps to question the order, dated 31.12.2020 passed by the respondent No.2 rejecting the objections or claim of the respondent No.6.
4 MSK,J W.P.NO.36006 OF 2022 6.

On the other hand, the respondent No.6 filed counter affidavit contending that in pursuant to the impugned letter, a reference was already taken on record by the said Authority and respondent No.6 herein has already filed a claim statement and the same is pending for adjudication, as such, Writ Petition filed before this Court is not maintainable.

The learned counsel for respondent No.6 also contended that entitlement or disentitlement of the petitioner as well as respondent No.6 can be adjudicated by the said Authority in pursuance to the reference made through the impugned letter.

He also contended that the appeals that were filed by the respondent No.6 before the respondent No.4 with regard to the various entries made in the revenue records in respect of subject property are pending for consideration and as such the issue can be well adjudicated by the said Authority instead of this Court going into those disputed questions of fact.
7.

There is no dispute that the objections/claim made by the respondent No.6 were rejected by the respondent No.2 by passing an order in proceedings R.C.No.A/7035/2016, dated 31.12.2020 and the said order has become final.
There is no challenge to the said proceedings as on date.
The only reason assigned by the respondent No.2 for referring the matter under 5 MSK,J W.P.NO.36006 OF 2022 Section 77(2) of the Act, 2013 to the Authority is pendency of W.P.No.13753 of 2020.
The said Writ Petition was already dismissed as withdrawn by order, dated 18.01.2023.

Even otherwise, mere pendency of the Writ Petition before this Court is not a valid ground for respondent No.2 to refer the matter under Section 77(2) of the Act, 2013, especially, in the absence of any challenge to the proceedings, dated 31.12.2020.

The counter affidavit, filed by the respondent No.2 herein in W.P.No. 13753 of 2020 is also placed on record and in the said counter affidavit, the respondent No.2 specifically contended that the objections raised by the respondent No.6 were already rejected by the respondent No.2 by passing an order dated 31.12.2020 and categorically stated that the respondent No.6 herein who is petitioner in W.P.No.13753 of 2020 has no right or title over the subject property.

8. The respondent No.2 having taken specific stand in the said Writ petition, instead of disbursing the compensation in favour of the petitioner herein, erroneously referred the matter under Section 77(2) of the Act, 2013 to the Authority on mere ground that W.P.No.17353 of 2020 is pending before this Court.
Such an action on the part of the respondent No.2 is wholly illegal and arbitrary.

In the absence of any order passed by this 6 MSK,J W.P.NO.36006 OF 2022 Court in the said Writ Petition, there is no justification for respondent No.2 to refer the matter under Section 77(2) of the Kadari Satayanarayana Reddy , ... vs The State Of Telangana on 9 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/21980004/
2 Act, 2013 that too, after having taken a specific stand that respondent No.6 has no right or title over the subject land.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Even during the course of the hearing of this Writ Petition also, this Court ascertained from the learned counsel for the respondents, as to whether respondent No.6 has taken any steps to question the order dated 31.12.2020 passed by the respondent No.2 and this Court is informed that the said proceeding was not challenged by the respondent No.6, as he has chosen to go before the said Authority under Section 77(2) of the Act, 2013 and participate in the said proceedings.

9. As the objections raised by the respondent No.6 were already rejected and the said order had become final, there is no justification for respondent No.3 in referring the matter once again under Section 77(2) of the Act, 2013, as there is no subsisting rival claim for compensation in respect of the subject land.

10. In the light of the above, this Court has no hesitation to hold that the action of the respondent No.2 in issuing impugned 7 MSK,J W.P.NO.36006 OF 2022 letter, dated 30.05.2022, as illegal and arbitrary and the same is liable to be set aside.
11. This Court after having arrived at the conclusion as noted herein above also made an effort to ascertain the basis and nature of the claim that is being set up by respondent No.6 herein.
A copy of the claim statement filed by the respondent No.6 before the authority pursuant to the reference made through the impugned letter is placed on record by the respondent No.6.

From the perusal of the said claim statement, it is noticed that according to the respondent No.6, the land in Sy.No.385 admeasuring Acs.11-34 guntas corresponding to the alleged survey No.448 originally belongs to one late Gona Venkata Mutyam Rao and after his demise, the said land is stated to have been devolved upon his only son, G.V. Raja Simha Rao, who died in the year 1997.

During his life time, one Beejohan Bee got entered her name in the revenue records in respect of the subject property and thereafter, the said Beejohan Bee sold the subject property in favour of the petitioner herein under registered sale deed, dated 10.09.2001 vide document No. 3217 of 2001 and he got entered his name in the revenue records by playing fraud.
The respondent No.6 herein claims to be the son of the said G.V.Raja Simha Rao.

From the very claim 8 MSK,J W.P.NO.36006 OF 2022 made by the respondent No.6 itself, it is evident that the name of the vendor of the petitioner herein was entered in the revenue records much prior to the year 1997 and petitioner has purchased the subject property through the registered sale deed in the year 2001 and his name has been continued as pattadar in respect of the subject property.
The respondent No.6 herein failed to take any action against the entries made in the revenue records in favour of the petitioner herein for the past more than twenty (20) years.
Therefore, the claim of the respondent No.6, if any, is totally belated, time barred and vague.

Except the claim statement and averments made in the counter affidavit, there is no other material placed on record to substantiate or prima facie satisfy this Court about the basis for the respondent No.6 to make a claim for payment of compensation in respect of the subject property.

12. In the light of the above, the impugned letter dated 30.05.2022 is liable to be set aside to the extent of referring the matter under Section 77(2) of the Act, 2013 to the Authority and the petitioner is entitled to receive the compensation as awarded through impugned letter/consent Kadari Satayanarayana Reddy , ... vs The State Of Telangana on 9 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/21980004/
3 award, dated 30-05-2022.
9 MSK,J W.P.NO.36006 OF 2022 13.

sentences.text:
Accordingly, the Writ Petition is allowed, thereby the impugned letter No. A/7035/2016-4, dated 30-05-2022 of the respondent No.4 in referring the claim relating to payment of compensation for acquisition of the petitioner's land in Sy.No.385 to an extent of Ac.0.14 guntas and Sy.No.385/A to an extent of Acs.5.08 guntas total land admeasuring Acs.5.22 guntas situated at Indaram Village,
Jaipur Mandal, Mancherial District under Section 77 (2) of the Act, 2013 to respondent No.2 is set aside.
Consequently, the petitioner is entitled to receive the compensation as awarded through impugned letter/consent award, dated 30.05.2022.

The respondent Nos.1 to 5 are further directed to take all necessary steps to pay compensation awarded through consent letter dated, 30.05.2022 together with interest accrued, if any as expeditiously as possible, at any rate, within a period of six (06) weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Miscellaneous applications, if any, pending shall stand closed.

(MUMMINENI SUDHEER KUMAR, J) Date:
